tone_statements.quote: Dhopadhola has two underlying level tones (tonemes): High (H) and Low (L) according to Kaplan (2007). The only contour tones in Dhopadhola are falling tones (HL and H!H), and they only appear on a phonological phrase –final syllable and on syllables with long vowels. [...] (p. 135:) Kaplan (2007) points out that Dhopadhola stress is fixed and falls on the root initial syllable of the word. The syllable structure of the language is (C) V (V) (C). [...] The stressed syllable is underlined; it falls on the stem initial syllable. Dhopadhola like Dholuo has two tones and both are active in the prosodic phonology of the language.
tone_statements.locator: sec. 3.2.2 'Dhopadhola Segmental and Prosodic Phonology', p. 51; sec. 5.2 (word-stress background), p. 135
tone_statements.summary: Two level tones H and L with falling contours restricted to phrase-final/long syllables (after Kaplan 2007), plus a claim of fixed stem-initial word stress.

tone_statements.citation: Kaplan, Aaron F. 2007. The Syllable as Contour Tone Host. Phonology at Santa Cruz (PASC) 7. Santa Cruz, CA: Linguistics Research Center, University of California, Santa Cruz. 24 pp.https://escholarship.org/uc/item/3sr39341
tone_statements.quote: Adhola has two tones, and both tones seem to be active in the phonology. (All data from Adhola come from my own notes from a field methods course taught at UC Berkeley in the fall of 2005.) That is, the contrast is between H and L rather than, say, H and ∅. The only contour tones in Adhola are falling tones (HL and H!H), and they only appear on phonological phrase-final syllables and on syllables with long vowels. [...] Under certain conditions, a high tone may spread rightward to an adjacent low-toned syllable.
tone_statements.locator: sec. 2 'Adhola', 2.1 'Spreading by Syllables', p. 4 (grammatical imperfective H: sec. 2.2, p. 8)
tone_statements.summary: Two level tones H and L on the syllable (syllable = TBU), lexical and grammatical (imperfective H prefixal tone), with rightward high-tone spread, downstepped H, and falling contours HL / H!H only on phrase-final or long-vowel syllables.

sources.note: No phonology, tone or stress content; references are Ethnologue, OLAC and ethnographic works (Oboth-Ofumbi 1959/1960, Ogot 1967).

sources.note: States that Dhopadhola has two underlying level tones H and L (citing Kaplan 2007), falling contours HL and H!H only phrase-finally and on long vowels, rightward H spread, PP-final vowel lengthening, downstep; gives Dhopadhola consonant and vowel inventories (17 consonants; [ATR] vowel pairs) and syllable types; additionally asserts fixed root-initial word stress for Dhopadhola (attributed to Kaplan 2007, who says nothing about stress) with a trochaic OT ranking, and reports that Dhopadhola listeners located English primary stress word-initially.

sources.note: First-hand OT analysis of Adhola tone: two tones H and L, both phonologically active (H vs L, not H vs zero); high tone spreading (HTS) proceeds syllable by syllable, so the syllable is argued to be the TBU; the only contour tones are falls (HL and H!H), restricted to phonological-phrase-final syllables and long-vowel syllables (phrase-final preconsonantal vowel lengthening feeds contours); downstepped H; a grammatical H tone is inserted at the left edge of imperfective verbs (wO!OlO 'is coughing' vs perfective); examples papali 'papaya' H-L-H > [pápâ:lí], oye:yo 'rat' L-H-L > [òyé:yô].
